# pranithjain.qzz.io - full catalog

> LLM-ingestible catalog of every tool, surface, and AI-agent endpoint on pranithjain.qzz.io. 
> This is a single concatenated document - every section is self-contained. The site has a live 
> DFIR + Threat Intel platform and an MCP server; the live endpoints are noted in their sections.

## Overview

Pranith Jain is an Associate Cyber Security Analyst on the Capgemini CERT team (Threat and
Vulnerability Intelligence group) working AI automation, autonomous workflows, and AI threat intelligence.
He builds and runs a live, edge-deployed DFIR and threat-intelligence platform at
https://pranithjain.qzz.io . The platform has three surfaces:

- A personal portfolio (/, /about, /skills, /experience, /projects).
- A 130+ tool DFIR toolkit (/dfir/*) covering IOC checks, phishing analysis, CVE triage, 
  Sigma/KQL/SPL/YARA rule conversion, email defense, IAM analysis, and more.
- A 124+ surface live threat-intelligence platform (/threatintel/*) with ransomware tracking, 
  IOC correlation, CVE/KEV feeds, actor timelines, breach monitoring, daily briefings, and an 
  autonomous case-study blog.

The platform is open at the edge - no signup, no API key required for browsing. Sensitive 
endpoints (admin, write operations) require an API key or admin token issued at /api/v1/admin/keys.

## DFIR toolkit tools (130+ routes)

- [DFIR Catalog](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/catalog) (dfir): Every DFIR tool, searchable, grouped by category.
- [IOC Investigator](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/ioc-investigate) (dfir): Cross-source investigation hub - paste any indicator type and pivot across all sources.
- [IOC Extractor](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/extract) (dfir): Pull IOCs from any text blob - refang-aware.
- [Certificate Transparency Monitor](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/ct-monitor) (dfir): Watch CT logs for new certificates matching your watchlist.
- [OSS Feed Registry](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/oss-feeds) (dfir): Curated catalog of 145+ free open-source threat intel feeds - IP, DNS, URL, hash, CVE, JA3, and more. Search by vendor, category, or keyword.
- [ORKL Library Search](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/orkl) (dfir): Search the ORKL open-source threat intelligence library - reports, actors, CVEs from hundreds of sources.
- [Traceix Hash Lookup](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/traceix) (dfir): SHA-256 hash reputation lookup via Traceix - per-engine antivirus/AV verdicts (Safe/Malicious/Unknown).
- [URL Risk Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/url-risk) (dfir): Multi-source URL risk scoring - static signals + VirusTotal, Safe Browsing, URLScan, AbuseIPDB and WHOIS-age correlation (IntelX framework port). 0-100 score with evidence chain.
- [Whoxy Reverse WHOIS](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/whoxy) (dfir): Reverse WHOIS lookup via Whoxy - find all domains registered by an email, name, company, or keyword.
- [Malware Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/malware-analyzer) (dfir): PE / ELF / Mach-O static analysis with import hashing + section entropy.
- [Infostealer Log Parser](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/stealer-parser) (dfir): Parse RedLine / Raccoon / Vidar / LummaC stealer logs - credentials, system, browser data.
- [Infostealer Intelligence](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/infostealer-intel) (dfir): Infostealer-specific intelligence dashboard - prevalent families, log types, and compromised credential tracking.
- [MalAPI](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/malapi) (dfir): Windows APIs abused by attackers - attack categories, libraries, and MS docs links.
- [Codec Hub](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/codec) (dfir): Decode and encode across base64, hex, URL, rot13, zlib, gzip with auto-detection.
- [Hash Calculator](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/hash-calc) (dfir): MD5 - SHA1 - SHA256 - SHA512 - SSDEEP - TLSH - drag a file in.
- [Timestamp Converter](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/timestamp) (dfir): Epoch - Windows FILETIME - Unix - human - bidirectional.
- [APK Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/apk-analyzer) (dfir): Manifest + permissions + signing certs + native libs.
- [EXIF / Metadata Parser](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/exif) (dfir): EXIF - IPTC - XMP - MakerNotes - camera, GPS, software fingerprints.
- [Plist & Protobuf Decoder](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/plist-protobuf) (dfir): Apple binary plist + protobuf human-readable view.
- [Punycode / Homoglyph Viewer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/punycode) (dfir): Visualise IDN homograph attacks - Cyrillic vs Latin lookalikes.
- [PowerShell Deobfuscator](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/powershell-deobf) (dfir): Unroll encoded / base64 / invoke-expression chains - step by step.
- [PowerShell Security Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/powershell-analyzer) (dfir): Static-analysis a PowerShell script for malicious behavior - 250+ signatures, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, IOC extraction, obfuscation scoring, risk score, 100% client-side.
- [File Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/file) (dfir): Upload a file - extract metadata, hashes, strings, and embedded indicators.
- [Hex Workbench](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/hex-workbench) (dfir): Browser-side hex viewer for artifact triage - inspect bytes, search hex/ASCII, jump to offsets, magic-byte family detection + entropy.
- [PCAP Triage](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/pcap-triage) (dfir): Protocol breakdown - top talkers - DNS / HTTP / TLS summaries.
- [Registry Hive Explorer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/registry-hive) (dfir): Browse - search - diff Windows registry hives offline.
- [EVTX Parser Lite](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/evtx) (dfir): Parse Windows Event Log files - event IDs, channels, time-range filter.
- [SQLite Artifact Explorer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/sqlite) (dfir): Browser profile - chat history - mobile backups - query in-browser via WASM.
- [iOS Backup Explorer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/ios-backup) (dfir): Manifest.db - plists - SQLite artifacts from a local iTunes backup.
- [Web Server Log Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/web-log) (dfir): Apache - nginx - IIS access logs - anomaly detection + pivots.
- [Prefetch Analyzer Lite](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/prefetch) (dfir): Parse Windows Prefetch files - execution evidence, run count, last run time.
- [Procedure Extraction](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/procedure-extract) (dfir): Threat report → reviewed x-procedure STIX bundles with Attack-Flow sequencing.
- [Windows Registry Artifacts Reference](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/winreg) (dfir): Windows Registry Forensic Artifact Reference - 292 artifacts, 16 categories, 10 hive types, 77 MITRE techniques.
- [Signature-Base YARA + IOCs](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/sigbase) (dfir): Neo23x0 signature-base - 746 YARA rule files (5,784 rules) + 4 IOC lists (hashes, C2, filenames, keywords).
- [DFIR Reference](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/dfir-ref) (dfir): Event IDs, memory forensics, browser artifacts, evidence collection phases — practitioner reference.
- [Chain of Custody Generator](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/coc-generator) (dfir): Build a defensible custody timeline — evidence inventory with hashes, transfer handlers, timestamps.
- [Domain Investigator](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/domain-investigator) (dfir): Cross-source domain investigation hub - 6 aliases route here (domain-rep, webcheck, etc.).
- [WHOIS History Explorer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/whois-history) (dfir): Historical WHOIS pivots - registrant, nameserver, status changes.
- [ASN Lookup](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/asn) (dfir): ASN details - prefix ranges - peer relationships.
- [Certificate Search](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/cert-search) (dfir): crt.sh-style CT log search for a domain - subdomains - cert chain.
- [DNSCOPE Infrastructure Map](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/dnscope) (dfir): 
- [Host Graph](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/host-graph) (dfir): Graph of related domains, IPs, and ASNs for a target.
- [Wayback Machine](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/wayback) (dfir): Search historical snapshots for a URL - changes over time.
- [Passive DNS](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/passive-dns) (dfir): Historical DNS resolution data for infrastructure tracking - migrations + fast-flux detection.
- [External Estate](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/estate) (dfir): ASN ownership and announced address space - the internet-facing footprint.
- [Asset Intelligence](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/asset-intel) (dfir): Aggregate asset inventory - domains, subdomains, services, certificates.
- [Exposed Host](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/exposed-host) (dfir): Per-host exposure score and evidence - services, versions, CVEs.
- [Open Directory Scanner](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/open-directory) (dfir): Detect misconfigured web servers exposing file listings.
- [URL Preview](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/url-preview) (dfir): Safe, sandboxed preview of a URL - headers, redirects, screenshot.
- [Subdomain Takeover Scanner](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/subdomain-takeover) (dfir): Detect dangling CNAMEs pointing to expired or unclaimed third-party services.
- [Exposure Analysis](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/exposure) (dfir): External attack surface exposure - open ports, services, certificates, and misconfigurations.
- [Email Defense](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/email-defense) (dfir): SPF / DKIM / DMARC / BIMI audit with failure modes called out.
- [Phishing Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/phishing) (dfir): URL + sender + header analysis with risk score.
- [DMARC Analyzer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/dmarc-analyzer) (dfir): Parse a DMARC aggregate report (RUA) - alignment, volume, failures.
- [EML Extractor](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/eml) (dfir): Headers - body - attachments - URL / hash extraction from a .eml file.
- [Email Reputation](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/email-rep) (dfir): Sender domain + IP reputation with deliverability signals.
- [Email OSINT Profile](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/email-osnit) (dfir): Build digital identity from email - GitHub, Gravatar, breach, reputation, DNS, PGP.
- [PhishBook](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/phishbook) (dfir): Curated playbook of phishing patterns, lures, and IOCs.
- [PHISHOPS](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/phishops) (dfir): Phishing-as-a-service operator catalog and tracking.
- [Username Investigator (alias)](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/username-investigator) (dfir): Alias of /dfir/username - the canonical page.
- [Phone Intelligence](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/phone-hub) (dfir): Phone number OSINT - carrier lookup, line type, breach presence, and AI-powered risk scoring.
- [Wi-Fi / BSSID Investigation](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/wifi-investigation) (dfir): Wireless network - BSSID vendor lookup, SSID analysis, security flags.
- [SOCMINT](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/socmint) (dfir): Social-media intelligence - X / Reddit / Telegram / Mastodon pivots.
- [OSINT Mapper](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/osint-mapper) (dfir): Build a mind-map of an investigation - nodes are entities, edges are pivots.
- [Breach Lookup](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/breach) (dfir): Email / username / domain - cross-correlate public breach corpora.
- [Image Intelligence](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/image-intel) (dfir): Image analysis - reverse search, perceptual fingerprinting, and OCR screenshot intelligence.
- [Brand Impersonation](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/brand-impersonation) (dfir): Detect typosquats / look-alike domains targeting your brand.
- [IntelligenceX Search](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/intelx) (dfir): Leaked data + phonebook search via IntelligenceX — emails, domains, BTC, IBANs, paste sites, breach archives.
- [Truecaller Lookup](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/truecaller) (dfir): Reverse phone lookup via Truecaller — caller name, carrier, spam score, and location data.
- [NHI Scanner](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/nhi-scan) (dfir): Inventory and risk-tier non-human & agent identities (service accounts, API keys, AI agents) against the OWASP NHI Top 10 - deterministic Tier 1-4 rules with least-privilege remediation for every finding.
- [CVE Lookup](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/cve) (dfir): Single-CVE detail - NVD, KEV, EPSS, exploit availability.
- [CVE Prioritizer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/cve-prioritizer) (dfir): CVSS + EPSS + KEV + ransomware-use - single patch-priority call.
- [CVE Resources Catalog](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/vuln-toolkit) (dfir): Curated list of CVE databases, exploit trackers, vendor PSIRTs.
- [OSV Dependency Scan](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/osv-scan) (dfir): Paste a manifest.json / package-lock / requirements.txt - known vulns.
- [CVE Risk Matrix](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/cve-risk-matrix) (dfir): CTI priority score (CVSS + EPSS + KEV + recency) plotted against CVSS — quadrant scatter plot + sortable table + SSVC-V decisions.
- [Fusion Exposure Worklist](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/fusion-exposure) (dfir): Composite 4-dimension scoring (CVSS/KEV/EPSS/Exploit-DB) - ranked worklist with per-dimension breakdown.
- [Risk Register](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/risk-register) (dfir): Full lifecycle CRUD with FAIR quantification, inherent->residual levels, and treatment plans.
- [Attack Path Graph](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/attack-path) (dfir): BFS shortest-path reachability from exposed assets to crown jewels - choke point detection, demo fallback.
- [GRC Compliance Evidence](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/grc-evidence) (dfir): Framework selector (SOC2/ISO27001/NIST/PCI/HIPAA), control tree, evidence collection with inline status.
- [Vulnerability Ops (VOC)](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/vulnerability-ops) (dfir): Intake / triage / SLA tracking - severity, status, source filters with auto-computed deadlines.
- [Ransomware Quantification](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/ransomware-quant) (dfir): Scenario-based financial impact across 7 cost dimensions with insurance recovery modeling.
- [Patch & Task Manager](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/patch-task-mgr) (dfir): Vendor advisory intake, maintenance window scheduling, approval workflows, deploy tracking.
- [SOC Automation Engine](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/soc-automation) (dfir): Playbook engine with configurable actions (webhook/email/slack/KB/MCP) - one-click execute, run history.
- [Rule Converter](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/rule-converter) (dfir): Sigma - KQL - SPL - YARA via one canonical IR.
- [YARA Workbench](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/yara-workbench) (dfir): Collaborative YARA editor with malware test corpus.
- [Threat Graph](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/threat-graph) (dfir): Indicator - relationship graph - visual pivot from any node.
- [Detection Chokepoints](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/detection-chokepoints) (dfir): Invariant detection points - prerequisites attackers cannot bypass, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
- [IR Playbooks](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/ir-playbooks) (dfir): Step-by-step playbooks for common incident types.
- [MITRE CAR](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/car) (dfir): Cyber Analytics Repository - validated detection analytics mapped to ATT&CK.

- [SIEM Use-Case Library](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/siem-library) (dfir): 60 detection use-cases across 16 categories — KQL + SPL starter rules with MITRE mapping.
- [Hunting Hypothesis Library](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/hunt-hypotheses) (dfir): 154 hunt hypotheses across 12 MITRE tactics — technique-driven, data-source-aware starter queries.
- [SOC Calculators](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/soc-calculators) (dfir): Alert fatigue index, SOAR ROI, EDR maturity, and log volume estimators.

- [Secret Scanner](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/secret-scan) (dfir): Scan a text blob / repo for API keys, tokens, private keys.
- [Medusa Scanner](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/medusa-scan) (dfir): AI-first security scanner - SAST (Python/JS/Go/Rust/PHP), secrets, prompt injection detection. 140+ rules, runs entirely in browser.

- [DLP Scan](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/dlp-scan) (dfir): Data-loss-prevention scan for files + clipboard + screenshots.

- [GRC Checklists](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/grc-checklists) (dfir): Control checklists for NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS v4, DPDP 2023, CERT-In, SEBI — plus cross-framework mapper.
- [Post-Quantum Cryptography](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/pqc) (dfir): Algorithm profiles, HNDL threat model, crypto-class readiness assessment, and migration checklist.
- [MITRE ATT&CK Navigator](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/attack-navigator) (dfir): Layered ATT&CK matrix - coverage heatmap, gap analysis.
- [Cyber Kill Chain](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/kill-chain) (dfir): Lockheed Martin 7-phase kill chain with ATT&CK cross-links.
- [Diamond Model](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/diamond) (dfir): Adversary - capability - infrastructure - victim - reference.
- [OWASP Top 10](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/owasp) (dfir): Web 2021 - API 2023 - LLM 2025 reference + checklist.

- [UTIOM — Operations Model](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/dfir/frameworks/utiom) (dfir): Unified Threat-Informed Operations Model v1.3 — 7 phases, 3 pillars, V-model validation. Interactive 7-phase self-check plus doctrine.

## MCP server (AI agent tools, 98 tools)

Endpoint: https://pranithjain.qzz.io/api/mcp (streamable HTTP)
Auth: Authorization: Bearer <api-key> or X-API-Key: <key>
Manifest: https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp-manifest.json
Drop-in configs: https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp/{claude-desktop,cursor,vscode-mcp}.json

- [ai_advisories](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): AI advisory firehose — per-package GHSA advisories, cvelistV5 CVE commits matched to known AI CVEs, tool release trains (garak, PyRIT, promptfoo, litellm, vllm, ollama, langchain, MCP SDK, MITRE ATLAS, OWASP GenAI), ExploitDB PoCs.
- [ai_playbook_cve_refs](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): CVE references cited by the AI Security Playbook, enriched against our local CISA KEV snapshot so you can see which are known-exploited. Enrichment comes from our own feed, never upstream.
- [ai_playbook_get_layer](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Get one AI Security Playbook division by roman id (I..VIII) or slug, including the risk identifiers it defines.
- [ai_playbook_get_risk_id](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Get one AI-security risk identifier by id (e.g. LLM01, ASI06), with its name, taxonomy and defining division.
- [ai_playbook_list_layers](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): List the 8 system divisions of the AI Security Playbook (I model .. VIII governance), with chapter counts and the risk identifiers each division defines.
- [ai_playbook_list_risk_ids](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): List the 20 AI-security risk identifiers: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (LLM01-LLM10) and the Agentic Security Index (ASI01-ASI10). Filter by scheme or layer, or search by id/name.
- [ai_playbook_stats](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): AI Security Playbook manifest stats: division/chapter/identifier counts, KEV matches, licence scope, and edge cache state.
- [ai_research](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): AI security research feed — Hacktron, Palo Alto Unit42, Cloud Security Alliance, BleepingComputer AI-filtered items with links back upstream.
- [ai_threats_get](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Return the full entry body for an AI-capable threat actor — includes full brief, aliases, raw TTP markdown, reported/activity dates, and MITRE technique IDs. Use ai_threats_list first to discover slugs.
- [ai_threats_list](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): List AI-capable threat actors from the Cybershujin tracker (79 entries, MIT). Each entry documents real-world confirmed use of AI/LLMs by threat actors. Filter by table (main/deepfake), category, TTP, or keyword.
- [ai_threats_stats](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Return cache + manifest stats for the AI Threat Actors data: total entries, index load state, body-cache hit ratios.
- [ai_vuln_get](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Full body for one AI vuln: description, references, aliases, affected packages, KEV dates, EPSS percentile. Call ai_vulns first to discover IDs.
- [ai_vulns](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Realtime AI vulnerability tracking — EUVD + NVD + OSV watchlist (litellm, vllm, langchain, mcp, transformers…), CISA/EU KEV overlap, FIRST EPSS exploit-probability. KEV-listed rows sort first.
- [analyze_phishing_email](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:phishing): Analyze raw email source for phishing indicators. Parses headers, checks SPF/DKIM/DMARC, extracts URLs, and computes a risk score with flags.
- [analyze_phishing_url](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:phishing): Analyze a URL for phishing indicators. Checks against PhishTank, OpenPhish, URLhaus, and performs visual similarity analysis.
- [analyze_report](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:analysis): Unified per-report analyzer. Runs summary + IOC extraction (with allowlist + confidence) + MITRE ATT&CK TTP mapping + 5W context + CVE extraction + image-OCR + STIX 2.1 bundle in a single round-trip. Accepts text, URL, or both; optionally takes image URLs to OCR. When format=markdown returns a TI Mindmap HUB-style rich formatted markdown report.
- [analyze_url_risk](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:phishing): Correlate a URL across VirusTotal, Google Safe Browsing, urlscan.io, AbuseIPDB, and WHOIS domain age using the weighted IntelX risk engine. Returns a 0-100 risk score, verdict (Critical/High/Suspicious/Low/No Strong Threat Evidence), confidence, static heuristic flags (punycode, shorteners, keywords, @-symbol, IP hosts), and a per-provider evidence chain with score breakdown.
- [anarchy_get_course](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Return the full body of a single Anarchy course by ID. Includes title, full description, tags, and external href. Use anarchy_list_courses first to discover IDs.
- [anarchy_list_courses](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): List courses from the Anarchy (kazamadono.github.io) portal — 1708 courses across 20 tracks (AI/ML, Low Level, PsyOps, Defensive, Offensive, OSINT, Game Hacking, BugBounty, Crypto, Reversing, Cloud, Forensics, CTF, Blockchain, IoT/HW, Dev/CS, Math). Filter by tag, difficulty, provider, hours, or free-text query. Daily sync from https://kazamadono.github.io/courses.json.
- [anarchy_recommend](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Rank Anarchy courses for a user library. Deterministic scorer (no LLM): tag affinity with saved/done/doing courses, same-provider affinity, and a difficulty ladder one rung above completed courses. Excludes library courses. Empty library returns beginner-friendly popular picks.
- [anarchy_similar](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Courses similar to one Anarchy course: shared tracks first, then same provider, then same difficulty. Use anarchy_list_courses first to discover IDs.
- [anarchy_stats](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Return cache + manifest stats for the Anarchy course catalog: course counts, top tags, sync timestamps, and LRU cache hit/miss ratios.
- [breach_vip_search](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:breach): Search the BreachVIP breach corpus (10B+ records, 1000+ datasets) directly. Supports 10 field types (email, username, domain, ip, phone, password, name, uuid, steamid, discordid). Returns grouped metadata: breach name, record count, and exposed data classes — raw credentials are never surfaced.
- [briefings_related](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Find prior briefings related to a given briefing — links by shared IOCs (domains/IPs/hashes/URL hosts) or shared tactic keywords, ranked by match count then severity then recency. Case-triage linkage (port of the CTI case-queue related-case matcher).
- [btc_abuse_check](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Check a Bitcoin address for abuse/scam reports on ChainAbuse. Returns the `verdict` field, which is authoritative: "flagged" means abuse reports exist, "clean" means the lookup completed and found none, and "unknown" means the lookup did NOT complete (missing CHAINABUSE_API_KEY or upstream error) — an "unknown" verdict is NOT evidence of a clean address and must not be reported as such. On "flagged", reports include categories (phishing, ransomware, scam, etc.), descriptions, and associated scam types. Useful for tracing illicit crypto transactions.

- [sigbase_stats](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:sigbase): Return cache + manifest stats for the Signature-Base data: YARA file/rule counts, IOC list/entry counts, external-variable rule files, and LRU body-cache hit/miss ratios.
- [soc_cve_report](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Generate a SOC CVE intelligence report. Takes a list of up to 50 CVE IDs and bundles CVE lookup + PoC scan + health check into a downloadable CSV or Markdown report. Returns executive summary, CVSS/EPSS/KEV details, PoC repos, and pipeline health.
- [static_triage_file](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Static file triage from base64 bytes (max ~6MB decoded): magic-byte family detection, hashes, entropy analysis, PE header parse, packer signals (UPX etc.), embedded artifacts (embedded PE/nested zip/OLE). No execution — pure structural analysis.
- [stix_query_bundles](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Query the STIX 2.1 intelligence bundle store with PostgREST-style filters. Returns threat intelligence bundles matching your criteria. Use stix_translate first to convert natural language to structured filter parameters. Supports filters: source_type (eq.osint/eq.darknet), threat_actors (cs.{APT29}), malware_names, sectors, countries_target, vulnerabilities, date ranges (stix_published_at=gte.), and more. Supports select, order, limit, offset.
- [stix_query_iocs](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Query the threat intelligence IOC store with PostgREST-style filters. Returns indicators of compromise with their type, validity period, and source bundle reference. Supports filtering by ioc_type (eq.ipv4, eq.domain, eq.hash_sha256), date ranges, and source. Also supports per-type active IOC queries via ioc_type filter. Use seq_id for incremental sync.
- [stix_translate](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Translate a natural language threat intelligence question into structured STIX 2.1 query parameters. Given plain English, returns the classified intent, extracted entities, and filter parameters to use with stix_query_bundles. Supports actors, malware, CVEs, sectors, countries, campaigns, time ranges, and strategic queries.

Filter by type, keyword, or minimum mention count. Each entry has a name, aliases, mention count, and first/last seen dates. Deterministic build-time extraction — no LLM in the loop.

Each IOC has a type, reason, first/last seen, and the source articles that reported it. Ready for firewall / Pi-hole / pfSense blocklists.

For each campaign: new domains, IPs, ASNs, cert issuers, page titles, and domains that went offline / came online within the window. Powers the "by the numbers" estate brief. Requires WEBAMON_API_KEY secret.
- [webamon_campaign_intel](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Webamon aggregated daily-brief digest in one call: global stats + top campaigns by 24h delta + change events in the window + emerging clusters, rolled up into "by the numbers" totals (new domains, takedowns, infra changes, new lure titles). Requires WEBAMON_API_KEY secret.
- [webamon_campaign_stats](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Webamon global estate rollup — total tracked campaigns, unique domains, online percentage, and aggregate activity. The headline numbers for the campaign-intelligence estate. Requires WEBAMON_API_KEY secret.
- [webamon_campaigns](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): List tracked phishing / malware-delivery campaigns from Webamon campaign intelligence (intel.webamon.com). Returns campaign cards with 24h domain delta, 7d activity, unique-domain totals, tags, and first/last seen. Sort by delta_24h to see the fastest-growing estates. Requires WEBAMON_API_KEY secret.
- [webamon_clusters](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Webamon emerging fingerprint clusters — groups of domains sharing a fingerprint (links/ssl/dom/domains/asn/scripts/tech) not yet promoted to tracked campaigns. Returns severity (critical/high/watch), unique-domain count, 24h delta, and the seed_query to pivot into search. Requires WEBAMON_API_KEY secret.
- [whoxy_reverse_whois](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Reverse WHOIS lookup via whoxy.com — find all domains associated with an email, owner name, company, or keyword. Searches 705M+ WHOIS records. Returns domain names, registrant info, and dates. Requires WHOXY_API_KEY secret.
- [wifi_investigation](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Investigate a wireless network by BSSID (MAC address) or SSID (network name). Returns OUI vendor lookup, MAC bit analysis (privacy/multicast), default SSID detection, WiGLE.net links, and security flags for rogue AP detection.
- [winreg_get_artifact](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:winreg): Return the full body of a single Windows Registry forensic artifact by slug. Includes registry keys, description, forensic value, parsers, and MITRE mapping. Use winreg_list_artifacts first to discover slugs.
- [winreg_list_artifacts](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:winreg): List Windows Registry forensic artifacts from the WinReg DFIR reference. Filter by category, hive, MITRE technique, or free-text keyword.
- [winreg_list_categories](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:winreg): List the Windows Registry artifact categories in the WinReg DFIR reference. Returns category keys, names, descriptions, and artifact counts.
- [winreg_stats](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:winreg): Return cache + manifest stats for the WinReg DFIR data: artifact counts, hive types, MITRE technique coverage, and LRU body-cache hit/miss ratios.
- [ws_add_connection](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Define a relationship between two subjects in a workspace.
- [ws_add_finding](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Log a finding with source, trust score, and confidence in a workspace.
- [ws_add_subject](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Register a subject (entity) in a workspace investigation.
- [ws_create](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Create a new investigation workspace for AEAD lifecycle tracking.
- [ws_export_stix](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Export workspace indicators as STIX 2.1 bundle or flat IOC list.
- [ws_exposure](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Calculate composite exposure score (0-100) for a target based on IOC reputation, breach exposure, infrastructure, attack surface, and threat intel.
- [ws_get](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Get a workspace with all subjects, connections, findings, and timeline.
- [ws_list](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): List investigation workspaces. Each workspace is a full AEAD-lifecycle case with subjects, connections, findings, and timeline.
- [ws_render_graph](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Render an ASCII box-drawing relationship graph, timeline, or risk heatmap from workspace data.
- [ws_workflow_advance](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Advance a workspace to the next AEAD phase (Acquire→Enrich→Assess→Deliver→Complete).
- [ws_workflow_summary](https://pranithjain.qzz.io/mcp) (mcp:other): Get workspace summary: phase progress, findings breakdown, recommended commands.

## Open-source packages published from this codebase

- cti-text-extract - synchronous, dependency-free CTI entity extractor.
- stix21-builder - STIX 2.1 bundle builder with deterministic UUIDv5 IDs.
- cti-ioc-enrich - pluggable IOC enrichment framework.
- telegram-preview-parser - parse Telegram channel previews to structured JSON.
- deepdarkcti-parser - parse the fastfire/deepdarkCTI markdown index to typed JSON.
- cti-platform - the threat-intel platform as a standalone app.
- DFIR-PLATFORM - the DFIR toolkit as a standalone app.
- cti-stix-connector (Python) - ingests CSV/JSON/MyThreatIntel data into valid STIX 2.1.
